name: Paul Creative Arts Center
use: Art & Art History, Music, Theatre & Dance; Johnson Theatre (667 seats), black box (Hennessy) theatre, recital rooms, studios
architect: Shepley, Bulfinch, Richardson and Abbott (principal Jean-Paul Carlhian); builder Harvey Construction
style: Mid-century modern; plain geometric brick forms on an E-shaped plan

renovations.what: Music wing extension built a few years after 1960 to designs by the original architects
First-floor music wing shut and fully refurbished after mold
Three-year life-safety project begun: new fire alarm throughout and sprinklers throughout; Hennessy Theatre done summer 2025, Johnson Theatre next, music wing from summer 2026 (Charters Brothers)

facts.text: Designed by Shepley, Bulfinch, Richardson and Abbott, with Jean-Paul Carlhian as principal architect, on an E-shaped plan with north and south wings joined by a central theatre/recital block.
Isabel and Harriet Paul gave $800,000 of the $2.5 million cost, then the largest gift in UNH history.
Dedicated October 13–15, 1960; built by Harvey Construction.
Facilities include a 667-seat proscenium theatre, a black box theatre, two recital rooms, practice rooms and art studios.
Campus master plans of 2004 and 2012 called an improved arts center a pressing need; a full renovation was estimated at $40–50 million in 2019.
In 2019 the building had no air conditioning and poor air circulation; mold forced a full refurbishment of the first-floor music wing in 2018.
Until 2025 the building relied on its original 1960 fire alarm and only partial sprinklers; a three-year life-safety project began in summer 2025.

verdict: 1960 SBRA arts centre with a patterned-brick fly tower; no A/C, a mold history and faculty who say it trails high schools.
notes: Photos (2013) show modest red-brick wings, a tall windowless brick fly tower with patterned brickwork, a gabled timber-clad theatre end; competent but plain; low-rise wings. A vintage postcard (card) gives 735 theatre seats versus 667 today. Museum of Art closure (Jan 2024, per old row) not re-verified here. Whether A/C has been added since 2019 is unconfirmed; the 2025 article mentions only fire systems. Old row's claim of accessibility work by Charters Brothers not verified. Ceiling height and daylight unknown.
judgeNotes: Photos show modest brick wings and a strong fly tower. Function and reputation low on faculty and student complaints.
